subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Big Bang: How It All Began
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Big Bang: How It All Began usable.

hook.text: 13.8 billion years ago, all matter, energy, space, and time erupted from a single point. That was the Big Bang.

buildup.text: It wasn't an explosion in space—it was an expansion of space itself. Every point in the universe was the center.

discovery.text: In the first second, quarks formed protons and neutrons. In three minutes, hydrogen and helium nuclei appeared.

twist.text: Nothing existed before the Big Bang—not even time. Asking 'what came before' may be a meaningless question.

climax.text: For 380,000 years, the universe was a glowing fog. Then it cooled enough for atoms to form, and light broke free.

punchline.text: No center, no edge. Space itself was born and is still expanding.

quiz.question: What does the Big Bang describe?
options: The expansion of space itself from an initial state
A massive explosion that happened somewhere in existing space
The collision of two universes that created our own

details.summary: The Big Bang theory describes the universe's origin from an incredibly hot, dense state approximately 13.8 billion years ago. Space itself expanded rapidly, cooling enough for particles, atoms, stars, and galaxies to form.
details.whyItMatters: The Big Bang is the foundation of modern cosmology — everything we observe follows from this event. Understanding it answers the most fundamental question humans have ever asked: how did the universe begin?
takeaways: The universe began 13.8 billion years ago from a hot, dense state
Space itself expanded — it was not an explosion in space
Particles, atoms, and galaxies formed as the universe cooled

faq.question: What evidence supports the Big Bang theory?
faq.answer: Three main pillars: the cosmic microwave background radiation (leftover heat from the early universe), the observed expansion of the universe (galaxies moving apart), and the abundance of light elements (hydrogen and helium in ratios matching predictions).

faq.question: What existed before the Big Bang?
faq.answer: This may be a meaningless question — if time itself began with the Big Bang, there was no 'before.' Some theories propose a multiverse, a prior collapsing universe, or quantum fluctuations in a vacuum. Currently, physics cannot describe conditions before the Planck time (10⁻⁴³ seconds).
